identity.title: The inhomogeneous submillimeter atmosphere of Betelgeuse

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present ALMA long (i.e., $\sim$16 km) baseline 338 GHz (0.89 mm) continuum observations of the free-free emission in the extended atmosphere of the M2 spectral-type supergiant Betelgeuse.

question.value: What is the thermal structure of Betelgeuse's extended atmosphere at ~1.3 R_star, and is it spherically symmetric or does it show localized heating?

evidence.quote: The mechanisms responsible for heating the extended atmospheres of early-M spectral-type supergiants are poorly understood.
(project code: 2015.1.00206.S, PI: P. Kervella)

analysis_steps.goal: Derive brightness temperatures and spectral index

method.value: Brightness temperature from fitted flux and size (Rayleigh-Jeans); spectral index from integrated flux in lower (331.86 GHz) and upper (344.09 GHz) band images; Eddington-Barbier Tb ~ Tgas

findings_qualitative.value: Emission is not spherically symmetric; localized heating likely tied to magnetic activity from convection

evidence.quote: We suggest that the detected localized heating is related to magnetic activity generated by large-scale photospheric convection.

claims.hypothesis: Is the mean temperature at ~1.3 R_star below the effective temperature (inversion)?
claims.experiment: Fit uniform disk to 338 GHz visibilities and derive Tb
claims.finding: Temperature inversion exists in the atmosphere of a red supergiant

evidence.quote: This is unambiguous proof for the existence of an inversion of the mean temperature in the atmosphere of a red supergiant.

claims.hypothesis: Is the sub-mm emission spherically symmetric?
claims.experiment: Images and visibility model fitting with residual inspection
claims.result: NE-peak (axis ratio 2.38, 3815 K) and east-extension detected

evidence.quote: Both emission asymmetries are clear evidence for localized heating taking place in the atmosphere of Betelgeuse.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Circular uniform disk and negative-flux Gaussians were rejected

evidence.quote: We also attempted fits by forcing the Gaussian components to have negative flux density values, but the fitted values were smaller than the fitting errors.

limitations_admitted.value: Limited resolution smears fine structures and reduces contrast; spectral index errors may be underestimated

evidence.quote: our limited spatial resolution would smear out these fine structures and would reduce the contrast in the brightness temperatures
